## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `clk`.
- Resets: `rst_n`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 5. Interfaces

- **s_axis_t*** - AXI4-Stream slave (input), tdata [PIX_W-1:0], tlast, tuser: interface `axis_if.slave` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`).
- **m_axis_t*** - AXI4-Stream master (output), tdata [PIX_W-1:0], tlast, tuser: interface `axis_if.master` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`).
- **r_s_axis_t*** - AXI4-Stream slave (input), tdata [PIX_W-1:0], tlast, tuser. tready = always 1: interface `axis_if.slave` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`).
- **r_m_axis_t*** - AXI4-Stream master (output), tdata [PIX_W-1:0], tlast, tuser: interface `axis_if.master` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`).

Bus ports follow the library's SystemVerilog interfaces, one definition file per type: AXI4-Stream `axis_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`, modports master / slave / monitor) and AXI4-Lite `axil_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv`, modports master / slave). Icarus Verilog cannot drive members of interface arrays and Yosys reads interfaces only through sv2v, so keep discrete ports (<prefix>_tdata, <prefix>_awaddr, ...) and put the interface and modport in a comment line directly above each port group: `// s_axis: axis_if.slave (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = 24`. Testbenches and Verilator flows may instantiate the interfaces directly.

| Port | Dir | Width | Group | Built when | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clk` | input | 1 | - | - | - |
| `rst_n` | input | 1 | - | - | - |
| `frames_o` | output | [31:0] | r_m_axis: axis_if.master (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = PIX_W | - | - |
| `drops_o` | output | [31:0] | r_m_axis: axis_if.master (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = PIX_W | - | - |
| `ret_drops_o` | output | [31:0] | r_m_axis: axis_if.master (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = PIX_W | - | - |

Back-pressure on every stream: honour tready, never drop data unless section 6 says so; valid must not depend combinationally on ready.

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
Glue between the video_pipeline insert point (a live camera
stream that must never stall for long) and vision_system (which captures
one whole frame, then generates the corrected frame, and accepts nothing
meanwhile). Version 1.0.0.
  - Frame admission: a frame is forwarded only when vision_system is
    ready (tready) and the return FIFO is empty (the previous corrected
    frame has gone on) at the moment its SOF pixel arrives; otherwise the
    whole frame is dropped (accepted and discarded) so the camera side
    keeps flowing. Pixels before the first SOF are dropped too, so
    vision_system always starts writing at a frame start.
  - Line gaps: vision_system needs >= barrel_pkg::LINE_GAP_CYCLES idle
    clocks between lines; GAP clocks are inserted after every forwarded
    tlast (default 8 = LINE_GAP_CYCLES 5 + 3; a design using
    vision_system passes barrel_pkg::LINE_GAP_CYCLES + 3).
  - Return path: vision_system's output does not support back-pressure
    (its bilinear datapath never stalls and it counts only accepted
    beats, so one refused beat would hang it in T_OUTPUT). Its
    m_axis_tready is therefore held high and the corrected frame goes
    through a RET_FIFO-word FIFO towards the pipeline. Admission only
    into an empty FIFO means RET_FIFO >= one frame (width x height)
    never overflows; should it still fill, the beat is dropped and
    counted (ret_drops_o) instead of hanging vision_system. For
    full-size frames use an external frame buffer (axis_dma + DRAM)
    here instead of on-chip RAM.
frames_o / drops_o count forwarded and dropped frames. Clock - clk.
Reset - synchronous rst_n (active low).
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the design.

```text
// Industry reference check - vs_stream_adapter (2026-10-16)
// Sources:
//   [1] Arm, "AMBA 4 AXI4-Stream Protocol Specification", ARM IHI 0051A (2010) / IHI 0051B
//   (2021), https://developer.arm.com/documentation/ihi0051/b - 2.2 handshake, 2.4 TKEEP /
//   TLAST
//   [2] AMD, "AXI4-Stream Video IP and System Design Guide", UG934 (2022),
//   https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/products/adaptive-socs-and-
//   fpgas/technologies/axi4-stream-video-ip-and-system-design-guide.pdf - TUSER(0) = SOF on the
//   first pixel, TLAST = EOL
// Published algorithm / equations:
//   AXI4-Stream: TVALID must not depend on TREADY (2.2.1: "a transmitter is not permitted to
//   wait until TREADY is asserted before asserting TVALID"); whole-frame drop decided at SOF
//   keeps frames intact.
// Comparison with this IP (section 6):
//   Matches: frame admission at SOF, whole-frame drop, line gaps. Open item from the code
//   review: admission currently looks at the downstream tready (to be replaced by a vs_idle_i
//   status, see code_reviews/vs_stream_adapter.sv_review.txt).
// TODO(REF-VS_STREAM_ADAPTER-1) [MEDIUM] Admission must not use tready. Prompt: in
//   ip/video/vs_stream_adapter/src/vs_stream_adapter.sv, decide frame admission from a
//   registered vision_system idle status input (vs_idle_i) and the return FIFO level instead of
//   m_axis_tready, so TVALID never depends on TREADY (IHI 0051 2.2.1); add a ready skid buffer
//   and update video_processor.sv to connect vision_system's idle status.
```


## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys.
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: Last Yosys synth_xilinx (7-series) result: about 49 LUTs, 152 flip-flops, 1 RAMB36E1. Stay within about this budget.

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

```text
Self-checking testbench for vs_stream_adapter (GAP = 6,
RET_FIFO = 64, 8 x 6 frames). A camera driver sends labelled frames on
s_axis; a behavioural vision_system model takes one whole frame on
m_axis (ready while idle and capturing), stays busy for a while, then
returns it on r_s_axis without looking at tready (as vision_system
does); the return side r_m_axis has random back-pressure. Checks:
reset state, pixels before the first frame start dropped, frames
forwarded whole and unchanged, at least GAP idle clocks after every
forwarded line, frames dropped while vision_system is busy or the
return FIFO is not empty (and the camera never held up while
dropping), the return path intact under back-pressure, and a return
FIFO overflow counted in ret_drops_o without stalling vision_system.
Prints TEST PASSED on success; +vcd dumps vs_stream_adapter_tb.vcd. The
test tasks are in tests/vs_stream_adapter_tests.sv (`included).
```

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `ip/scripts/run_sim.sh vs_stream_adapter --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `vs_stream_adapter_tb` | `test_reset` | Counters 0, no output valid, r_s_axis_tready high after reset |
| `vs_stream_adapter_tb` | `test_leading_pixels` | Pixels before the first frame start are dropped, then the frame is forwarded |
| `vs_stream_adapter_tb` | `test_forward` | A frame sent while vision_system is idle is forwarded whole and unchanged and returned |
| `vs_stream_adapter_tb` | `test_line_gap` | At least GAP idle clocks after every forwarded line |
| `vs_stream_adapter_tb` | `test_drop_busy` | A frame arriving while vision_system is busy is dropped (drops_o) without holding up the camera, and the next one is forwarded |
| `vs_stream_adapter_tb` | `test_drop_return_full` | A frame arriving while the return FIFO still holds the previous corrected frame is dropped |
| `vs_stream_adapter_tb` | `test_return_backpressure` | Ten frames with 50 % back-pressure on the return side: every forwarded frame returned intact, none lost (ret_drops_o 0) |
| `vs_stream_adapter_tb` | `test_ret_overflow` | More return beats than the FIFO holds with the return side stopped: vision_system is never stalled, the excess is counted in ret_drops_o and the beats kept come out in order |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

Pass criteria: `make -C video/vs_stream_adapter test` passes, every coverage target met, Verilator lint clean, `sv_format.py --check` clean, `make synth` passes.
